clue.text: See 2
Sit down, shut up and listen! Wiglaf ruled fairly in defence of Nuremberg

definitions.text: Sit down, shut up and listen! Wiglaf ruled fairly in defence of Nuremberg

parts.words: Sit down, shut up and listen! Wiglaf ruled fairly in defence of Nuremberg
parts.note: the setter's name gives the first person and 'ruled fairly' gives was just; this statement sits straight after a string of three commands, so in the clue it comes after the instructions, and the whole is the plea made at the post-war trials

explanation.surface: A shouted call to order in a courtroom, then the setter claiming his verdicts were fair, in a war-crimes trial setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own layout is the joke: the claim about Wiglaf being fair literally comes after a run of commands. 'ruled' looks like governing; here it is just 'was'.
explanation.definitionFit: Defendants at the post-war Nuremberg tribunals famously pleaded that they had merely obeyed superiors, a plea now known by this phrase.

clue.text: Group knocked over non-alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the letters are read in the opposite direction in this down clue
drinks means takes in, so the word non-alcoholic holds a short run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A party of teetotallers clumsily tipping over their soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of families sharing descent, so the word works as a plain synonym for a group.

clue.text: Engineer runs over Saudi national, a reactionary fellow

indicators.note: to engineer something is to contrive or arrange it, so these letters are set out anew

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An engineer driving over a Saudi citizen, who turns out to be a reactionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a fossil-age creature is someone hopelessly old-fashioned who resists change, so the idiom fits a reactionary man.

clue.text: Generally, not all divers go

indicators.note: not marks the letters of all as ones to be taken away from the longer word
divers is an old word for various or assorted, so the remaining letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that, as a rule, only some scuba divers go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like people under water; it is the archaic adjective meaning sundry. Taking A, L, L out of GENERALLY leaves GENERY, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Go in the sense of vigour or get-up-and-go is a synonym for liveliness and drive.

clue.text: Clergymen in crowd endlessly pinching behind

indicators.note: pinching means taking hold of, so one piece is held inside the other
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to crowd is to press, as a throng does
behind in the sense of overdue is late

explanation.surface: A pickpocket in a throng nipping someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a backside but means overdue. 'endlessly' trims the last letter, giving PRES, and 'pinching' wraps that round LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prelates are senior churchmen such as bishops, so they are a class of clergymen.

clue.text: Description of centre for refreezing hydrocarbon

definitions.text: Description of centre for refreezing hydrocarbon

parts.words: Description of centre for refreezing hydrocarbon
parts.note: the two middle letters of the ten-letter word refreezing are an E followed by another E; describing that in words spells the name of a simple gas made of carbon and hydrogen

explanation.surface: A technical account of the gas at the core of a refrigeration plant.
explanation.walkthrough: REFREEZING has ten letters, so its centre is letters five and six, both E: putting into words what is there, one E then another E, spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethene, also called ethylene, is a simple gas made only of carbon and hydrogen, so it is an example of a hydrocarbon.

clue.text: After revolution in Kyiv, in retrospect, one's left bankrupt

indicators.note: after a revolution things have been turned upside down, so these letters are scrambled
left signals that the letter for one is left over once the answer has been made

parts.note: taken as written as the pool of letters
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: After Ukraine's uprising, someone looking back finds themselves left without money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After revolution' and 'left' are the indicators: the letters of KYIV IN RETROSPECT, less one I, are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is bankrupt has no money left at all, which is the state of extreme want described by the compound adjective.

clue.text: Blair's alien world finally lost battle

indicators.note: a battle is a mêlée in which everything is thrown together, so these letters are reordered
finally lost says that the last letter of world is removed

explanation.surface: A sci-fi tale of a politician's extraterrestrial planet losing a war at the last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' looks like Tony Blair; it is Eric Blair, the real name of George Orwell. 'finally lost' takes D from WORLD, leaving WORL to mix with ALIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to or characteristic of the writer whose birth name was Eric Blair.

clue.text: 5 mph to 100 mph? That's some acceleration

indicators.note: some says only part of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: A car going from walking pace to motorway speed: impressive acceleration.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 mph to 100 mph' reads as a speed increase, but it is one quantity compared with another, one to twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Two quantities expressed as one to another, like 5 to 100, form a proportion of this kind.

clue.text: Ukrainian pseudoscientist modified extremists in Kabul? Yes and no

indicators.note: modified means altered, so these letters are rearranged
extremists are those at the very ends, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: A question about whether radicals in Afghanistan's capital have changed, answered with a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists in' takes K and L from Kabul, which are mixed with YES and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Trofim Lysenko was a Soviet agronomist born in Ukraine whose rejection of genetics is the classic case of state-backed bogus science.

clue.text: Remember to secure terminal in game console

indicators.note: to secure means to enclose or hold fast, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to remember an experience vividly is to relive it

indicators.note: terminal means at the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A reminder to plug something into the port of a games machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'console' looks like the games machine; it is the verb meaning to comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to ease their distress, which is to relieve them of worry or grief.

clue.text: Couples involved centrally in swap duly cry

indicators.note: couples are pairs of letters, and centrally says the pair at the middle of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Partners in a wife-swapping arrangement who duly end up in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To waul is to give a plaintive cat-like wail, an old verb related to caterwaul, so it is a kind of crying out.

clue.text: 'The Life of Riley' could be clue for setter

parts.note: read the second half as an anagram clue: an indicator meaning loose or comfortable followed by fodder that rearranges to give the word setter

explanation.surface: A setter musing that a famous phrase about comfort would make a good clue.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer is itself a tiny clue, with 'easy' as an anagram signal working on STREET, whose letters give SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe a life of comfort and affluence free from worry or financial hardship.

clue.text: More crazy headline, following split

indicators.note: after being split into its two halves, each half of the word headline is swapped for a slang or everyday synonym

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline made even madder once a story about a separation breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Split HEADLINE into HEAD and LINE: NUT is slang for the head and a TIER is a line or row, one rank above another.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of the informal adjective for mad means crazier, so it means more crazy.

clue.text: Satellite network put on the work of Gilbert and Sullivan

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons, a natural satellite
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A satellite broadcaster screening a Gilbert and Sullivan production.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe is one of the comic operas written by the librettist Gilbert and composer Sullivan.

clue.text: Multi-purpose transport's possible, but with difficulty fitting inside

indicators.note: fitting inside means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: poss is an informal short form of possible

indicators.note: done with difficulty suggests the letters are twisted into a new shape

explanation.surface: A comment that a versatile vehicle can just about squeeze something in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural mail van that also carries passengers serves both purposes, delivering letters and providing transport.

clue.text: Some geek's daughter going West and East?

parts.note: some of something is a part of it

indicators.note: going means departing, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a geek is a nerd, and the possessive supplies the S

explanation.surface: A nerd's daughter travelling around the world in both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West and East' look like compass points or travel; in bridge they are the two players who sit opposite and play together.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, the players in the West and East seats form one pair playing against North and South.

clue.text: Elizabeth and Edward getting so involved is foolish

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Bet is a pet form of the name Elizabeth
Ted is a pet form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A couple, Elizabeth and Edward, getting so wrapped up in each other that it looks silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides infatuated, the word can mean muddled or stupefied, as by drink, so it overlaps with foolish.

clue.text: Everybody goes through broken sunroof, crawling?

indicators.note: goes through means passes into the middle of something
broken means smashed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: everybody is all

explanation.surface: A whole family climbing in through a smashed car sunroof on their hands and knees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes ONFOURS, which 'goes through' splits so ALL sits in the middle. The question mark marks crawling as an example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving on hands and knees is the posture of a crawling baby, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Yellow fruit, not black fruit

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: bananas are the familiar yellow-skinned fruit
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fruit seller distinguishing yellow produce from the dark sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the pineapple, from the Tupi name, used in many European languages and in older English, so it is a fruit.

clue.text: Mathematics student's work schedule

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
to schedule something is to time it

explanation.surface: A maths undergraduate's timetable of assignments.
explanation.definitionFit: At Cambridge, a senior or junior optime is a student placed in the second or third class of the mathematics Tripos.

clue.text: Heads off to Syrian Arab Republic to see ruler

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Leaders setting off to Syria to meet its head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, so the title names a supreme ruler.

clue.text: Police search transvestite attire and lace

parts.note: drag is clothing of the opposite sex worn for performance
lace is a fine open fabric, a kind of net

explanation.surface: Officers searching a wardrobe of drag outfits and lacy items.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragnet is a coordinated, wide-ranging police operation to catch a suspect, named after a fishing net dragged along the bottom.

clue.text: Relatively partial to nice bit of pie freshly baked

indicators.note: something freshly made has been put together anew, so these letters are rearranged
a bit of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone who has a weakness for a slice of hot pie straight from the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively partial' looks like 'fairly keen'; read as 'partial to relatives', it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism shown to family members, so the adjective describes bias towards one's relatives.

clue.text: £25 a glass?

definitions.meaning: British slang for twenty-five pounds sterling is a small horse's name
a small measure of beer or spirits, by the same name as a small horse

explanation.surface: Outrage at the cost of a single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word is twenty-five pounds, and it also names a small glass or measure of drink.

clue.text: Enormous bird eating a husband's fish

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird from Arabian legend
H is the abbreviation for husband; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A huge bird swallowing a man's catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The roach is a common European freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Around lunchtime, sailor has entrée for starters served in white wine and onion sauce

definitions.text: served in white wine and onion sauce

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the sailor goes round the other piece

parts.note: a sailor is a mariner
lunchtime is one o'clock, and I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: for starters means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor at a midday meal ordering a starter of mussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrée' and 'starters' look like courses of the meal; one is the fodder and the other the signal for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary term, as in moules marinière, describes dishes cooked in white wine with onions and herbs.
